title: Experimental History
lead: Why a condensate in a gas came so late: superfluid helium, a condensate with a strong quantum depletion; the metastable state a gaseous condensate must be; spin-polarized hydrogen and the walls that stopped it; and the stability window in which laser-cooled alkali atoms can be evaporatively cooled.
notes: Figure 11.1 is redrawn as the book draws it, a still faithful copy.

figures.original_caption: Allowed and forbidden regions of temperature and density, shown with the BEC critical temperature $T = T_c(n)$ (qualitative).

footnotes.html: The book prints “the metastable triplet state of hydrogen”. Meant is the triplet state of a pair of hydrogen atoms whose electron spins are parallel: their interaction potential holds no bound state, so the pair cannot form $H_2$.
